desc:
You work in a single room. Each requested meeting is a half-open range [start, end). You may accept any subset of the requests, but between two accepted meetings the room needs a break: if one accepted meeting ends at time e and the next accepted one starts at time s, then s - e ≥ buffer.

Return the largest number of meetings you can accept.

meetings = [[1, 3], [3, 5], [6, 8], [8, 10]], buffer = 0  ->  4
meetings = [[1, 3], [3, 5], [6, 8], [8, 10]], buffer = 1  ->  2
constraints: The requests are in no particular order
hints: With buffer = 0 this is the classic activity-selection problem. Recall which greedy rule solves it.
Accepting the meeting that ends earliest leaves the most room for the rest. The buffer simply moves the point after which the next meeting may start.
Sort by end time. Keep the end of the last accepted meeting; accept a meeting if its start is at least lastEnd + buffer, then update lastEnd.
editorial: Exchange argument: among all meetings that are compatible with what is accepted so far, the one with the earliest end leaves the largest remaining window, and any optimal schedule can be changed to start with it without losing a meeting. The buffer only changes the compatibility test from s ≥ lastEnd to s ≥ lastEnd + buffer; the exchange argument still holds because replacing a meeting by one that ends no later can only make the next gap larger.
Sort by end time (ties do not matter), sweep once and count. The sort gives O(n log n) time and O(n) space. Be careful with 32-bit overflow in other languages: lastEnd + buffer can reach 2·109.
